thesis: Micron's ~18% 60-day decline coincides with a broad semiconductor sector selloff tied to renewed U.S. chip-tariff uncertainty and two unresolved litigation overhangs -- an August 12, 2026 Netlist ITC patent complaint targeting DDR5 RDIMM/MRDIMM products and a June 2026 DRAM price-fixing antitrust suit naming Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix -- rather than any confirmed deterioration in company-disclosed fundamentals. Micron's most recent quarter showed record cash (~$30.2B), reduced debt, and management commentary that 2026 output capacity is largely already sold, which suggests the pullback is more macro/litigation-sentiment driven than earnings-driven. Both litigation matters remain early-stage and unresolved, leaving a live overhang heading into Micron's fiscal Q4 2026 earnings report on September 30, 2026, which functions as a binary catalyst that could confirm or reverse this read.
invalidation: Invalidated if the Netlist ITC investigation is instituted with a schedule indicating a likely import exclusion order against Micron products, if the DRAM price-fixing antitrust suit survives a motion to dismiss and advances toward material liability, or if the September 30, 2026 fiscal Q4 earnings/guidance show actual demand, pricing, or margin deterioration rather than sentiment-driven weakness.

thesis: MRVL's ~13% 60-day decline predates its Q2 FY27 earnings and largely reflects a sector-wide AI/semiconductor valuation reset, not a company-specific negative event. Q2 FY27 results (reported Aug 27, 2026) beat consensus with record $2.74B revenue (+37% YoY) and raised FY27/FY28 guidance, yet shares fell further because Q3 gross-margin guidance stepped down sequentially on a mix shift toward lower-margin custom AI silicon, disappointing a stock that had traded near 64x earnings after a 179%+ YTD run. This suggests the move is primarily a valuation/expectations reset layered on genuinely strong and improving fundamentals, though a recently disclosed Google warrant (up to ~59M shares, Aug 19 2026) adds real ongoing dilution risk to the share count.
invalidation: Invalidated if Q3 FY27 results (expected ~November 2026) miss the guided $3.15B revenue / $1.10 EPS, if non-GAAP gross margin falls meaningfully below the 57.5% floor without a credible recovery path, if Google or other custom-silicon partners signal order deferral or cancellation, or if sector-wide AI-capex sentiment fails to stabilize and multiple compression continues independent of Marvell's own results.

thesis: NVIDIA's ~17% two-month price move is explained by a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: Q2 FY2027 results (reported Aug 26, 2026) beat consensus on revenue ($96.22B vs. $92.07B expected) and EPS ($2.22 vs. $2.09 expected), with Q3 FY2027 guidance of $108.0B also above Street estimates, marking a 13th consecutive quarterly guidance beat. This suggests continued strong AI-infrastructure demand is driving the move rather than macro or technical factors alone. However, the read is complicated by unresolved risks not addressed by the earnings beat: a certified securities class action tied to historical revenue-disclosure claims, an unresolved Chinese antitrust probe over Mellanox-deal compliance, and ongoing concerns about circular AI financing arrangements and customer concentration.
invalidation: Invalidated if hyperscaler/AI-infrastructure capex growth decelerates materially, if China's SAMR issues a material fine or additional export restrictions materially impair China-related revenue, if the certified securities class action produces an adverse ruling, settlement, or discovery disclosure indicating undisclosed material risk, or if a future quarter breaks the multi-year streak of guidance beats.

thesis: The ~12% 60-day rise coincides with Apple's confirmed fiscal Q3 2026 results (reported July 30, 2026): record revenue of $109.4B (+16% YoY), iPhone revenue up 22% YoY for a third straight quarter, EPS up 28.7%, and a $100B buyback authorization, suggesting the move reflects real company-specific operating momentum rather than pure sentiment or a macro/sector move. This confirmed strength coexists with unresolved live risks disclosed by the company itself: management flagged a 'hundred-year flood' in memory-chip pricing pressuring gross margins into the September quarter, and the EU has an open DMA Article 6(4) investigation with an October 1, 2026 compliance deadline carrying potential fines up to 10% of global revenue. A first-time CEO (John Ternus, effective September 1, 2026) also takes over just ahead of the September 9 product launch, adding execution uncertainty during the near-term catalyst window.
invalidation: A disappointing September 9 iPhone/foldable launch reception, an adverse EU DMA compliance outcome or fine after the October 1, 2026 deadline, or fiscal Q4 2026 earnings (expected late October) showing memory-cost margin erosion worse than guided under the new CEO would invalidate this thesis.

thesis: The 60-day decline coincides with multiple disclosed, company-specific overhangs rather than one clean catalyst: mechanical share-supply pressure from post-IPO lockup unlocks (911.5M shares Aug 6, another ~319M Aug 20, final tranche not freeing until Dec 8, 2026), a Sell-rated analyst downgrade citing valuation and dilution risk, disclosed heavy cash burn ($16B in Q2) with free cash flow not expected positive until 2029, and an FAA-mandated grounding of Starship testing following a May 2026 booster mishap that has not yet resolved. A credible bull case exists (92% YoY revenue growth, profitable Starlink, fast-growing AI segment, Morgan Stanley Overweight rating well above the current price) but it depends on still-unproven future execution, so the setup remains a live, unresolved risk rather than a confirmed positive resolution.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Starship Flight 14 (targeted mid-to-late September 2026) completes successfully with full FAA return-to-flight clearance, and if the Q3 2026 earnings report shows a credible narrowing path toward positive free cash flow with no further large dilutive raises.

thesis: Intel's ~30% 60-day decline reflects a confluence of disclosed, company-specific structural pressures -- a $20B dilutive equity offering priced within the last 90 days, continuing multibillion-dollar Foundry operating losses guided through 2027, and x86 CPU market share falling to a 31-year low against AMD -- layered on a broader semiconductor sector selloff. Data Center/AI revenue growth and CEO insider buying at the offering price suggest some fundamental support, but this is offset by unresolved shareholder litigation over the U.S. government's equity stake and unproven 18A/Foundry profitability, leaving the evidence mixed rather than clearly resolved in either direction.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Intel Foundry demonstrates a credible path to breakeven ahead of the 2027 guided timeline, x86 CPU share versus AMD stabilizes or reverses, and the federal derivative litigation over the government stake is dismissed or settled without a fiduciary-breach finding.

thesis: AMD's ~12% two-month decline coincides with a broader semiconductor/AI-capex sentiment selloff and valuation compression (shares had rallied ~126% YTD to roughly 120x trailing earnings before pulling back) rather than any adverse company-disclosed event -- Q2 2026 results beat expectations with record revenue of $11.55B (+50% YoY) and Q3 guidance called for ~$13B revenue (+41% YoY). No active litigation, accounting restatement, or execution-related C-suite exit was found. AMD's disclosed compute-for-equity warrant deals with OpenAI and Meta (up to 320 million shares, roughly 20% of shares outstanding) plus a record $4.75B August 2026 debt raise represent a confirmed, material dilution and leverage overhang layered on otherwise strong fundamentals.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if Q3 2026 earnings (due Nov 3, 2026) show decelerating data-center/AI revenue growth or gross-margin compression below the guided ~56%, if a formal SEC/DOJ investigation or securities class action naming AMD is disclosed, or if OpenAI/Meta warrant vesting accelerates and materially dilutes EPS faster than shipment milestones currently imply.

thesis: Dell's approximately 14% 60-day rally coincides with specific, company-disclosed developments: Dell was named technology provider on a $10 billion AI-factory deal (disclosed August 4, 2026), and the company reported a record $51.3 billion AI server backlog and raised its FY27 AI server revenue outlook to roughly $60 billion, prompting several sell-side price-target increases -- suggesting the move reflects company-specific AI-infrastructure demand strength rather than macro or sector-wide sentiment. No disclosed accounting irregularity, executive misconduct, dilutive equity/convertible raise, insolvency indicator, or operationally-driven leadership departure was found, and existing litigation (an ERISA 401(k) suit and a server-pricing dispute) carries no scheduled ruling within the next 90 days. Dell reports Q2 FY27 earnings on September 1, 2026 -- a live, unresolved binary event that could confirm or reverse the current read on backlog conversion and guidance, which is why this is capped at medium rather than high conviction.
invalidation: A material miss on Q2 FY27 revenue/EPS versus the ~$44-45B/~$4.80-4.95 consensus, a downward revision to the AI server backlog or the ~$60B FY27 AI revenue outlook, or evidence that supply constraints are preventing backlog-to-revenue conversion, disclosed at or after the September 1, 2026 earnings report.

thesis: Affirm's August 27, 2026 fiscal Q4 earnings showed revenue of roughly $1.16-1.17B (+33% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $4.62, both well above consensus, plus raised FY2026 guidance and an 11th consecutive quarter of 30%+ GMV growth, which suggests today's volume spike reflects a genuine, company-specific fundamental catalyst rather than rumor, macro sentiment, or technical positioning. However, an active consumer class action (Shepard v. Affirm Holdings, SDNY) alleging deceptive BNPL marketing remains in court-supervised mediation with reported potential liability above $500 million, and analysts continue to flag rising early-stage delinquencies among subprime/near-prime borrowers as an unresolved credit-quality risk.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if Affirm's next quarterly report (expected ~November 2026) shows GMV/revenue growth decelerating meaningfully below the ~30%+ trend, delinquencies/credit losses rising materially beyond current allowance levels, or if the pending Shepard v. Affirm consumer class action produces an adverse ruling or settlement imposing material financial or operational constraints.

thesis: Tenable's 60-day uptrend is grounded in a confirmed, company-disclosed Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised FY2026 revenue and EPS guidance (reported ~Aug 6, 2026), alongside record Tenable One platform adoption and improving net dollar expansion. Today's outsized volume spike is explained by S&P Dow Jones Indices' confirmed Aug 26, 2026 announcement that TENB will join the S&P SmallCap 600 effective Aug 31, 2026, replacing Leggett & Platt, which suggests continued near-term passive-fund demand for the stock even though that portion of the move reflects mechanical index-rebalancing flows rather than new operating information. No litigation, restatement, dilution, solvency, or leadership-turnover red flags were found.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if TENB gives back a substantial portion of its post-announcement gain in the days/weeks after the Aug 31, 2026 S&P SmallCap 600 effective date once passive-fund rebalancing flows are complete, or if Q3 2026 results show billings/NDER deceleration that undercuts the raised FY2026 guidance.

thesis: SUNB's 6.3x volume spike on Aug 28, 2026 lines up with a broad macro/rate-driven risk-off session (hot July PCE inflation, 10-year Treasury yields above 4.65%, and a Fed Chair Jackson Hole speech that day) rather than any single new company-disclosed catalyst. This sits on top of an 11-month streak of declining nonresidential construction spending and a Q4 FY2026 EBITDA margin miss that drove JPMorgan and BofA price-target cuts, while an active federal antitrust MDL alleges Sunbelt Rentals, United Rentals, and Herc coordinated pricing through the Rouse data platform, still in active proceedings. Wells Fargo's Overweight initiation and an ongoing $1.5B buyback offer some offsetting support, but the evidence remains mixed and largely macro/sentiment-driven rather than a confirmed company-specific event.
invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated if Q1 FY2027 results (Sept 9, 2026) show EBITDA margin stabilization and rental rate/volume reacceleration, nonresidential construction spending data turns positive, or the antitrust MDL is dismissed with prejudice as to Sunbelt Rentals.

thesis: ESI's 60-day decline and today's 5.78x volume spike trace to the confirmed, mutually agreed termination (Aug 27, 2026, per SEC 8-K) of the previously announced $14.5B Solstice Advanced Materials merger, which both companies attributed to shareholder feedback rather than any diligence, financial, or regulatory problem, with no breakup fee owed by either side. Element Solutions reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance and posted record Q2 net sales (+56% YoY, beating consensus by 11.5%) around the same period, and sell-side analysts (RBC, UBS) characterized the termination as a positive for equity holders. This suggests the sharp price/volume move largely reflects merger-arbitrage position unwinding around a confirmed corporate event rather than newly disclosed fundamental deterioration, even though the stock's historically rich standalone valuation and its continued slide the day after termination remain a live risk not yet tested by an earnings cycle.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if ESI's Q3 2026 results (expected mid-to-late October 2026) miss reaffirmed guidance or guidance is cut, or if the stock continues falling meaningfully below its pre-merger-announcement level (~$46.30 on 2026-06-29) after merger-arbitrage-related selling has had time to clear.
